comment: Real Rails apps with recorded resolution baselines. Not run by test/run_all.rb --
that suite is hermetic and must stay fast. Run this deliberately:
Each entry is pinned to a ref, because a baseline against a moving target means
nothing. Re-pin and re-measure together, never separately.
Floors sit a little below the measured value: they are regression detectors, not
exact-match assertions, and a repo gaining models should not fail the suite.
To add one: clone, pin the ref, run --diagnose, hand-check every unresolved
association against the source, then record what remains as the baseline. The
hand-check is the part that matters -- it is what turns a number into evidence.

repos.name: docuseal
repos.notes: Rails 7, 304 files, 34 models. The repo D1-D6 were found in, so its numbers are the weakest evidence the fixes generalise -- a regression guard, not a validation set.

repos.name: mastodon
repos.notes: Rails 8, 248 models, 18 custom acronyms, ActiveModel::Serializer throughout. Found F1 (serializer macros), F2 (with_options), F3 (compound irregulars), F5 (lib/ not autoloaded). Measured 95% after fixes: the 21 remaining are 6 Doorkeeper gem models and 15 deliberate has_many :through far-end guesses.

repos.name: solidus
repos.notes: Engine monorepo -- seven gems, each with its own app/ and gemspec. Found F6 (gemspec-marked engine roots: this resolved to ZERO autoload roots before), F7 (inflections in a gem's initializers and inside engine.rb), F8 (constant assignment as definition), F9 (root-scoped `class ::Foo::Bar`). Went 54% -> 95%.

repos.name: chatwoot
repos.notes: Flat Rails app with an enterprise/ overlay added via eager_load_paths. The only corpus repo that passed on first contact, at 97% -- which is the point of having one the tool was not tuned against. Its enterprise/app/** paths are still not read; see open-questions Q4.
